title: FreshRSS
wrapper_note:
the official entrypoint needs root (timezone symlink, sed on /etc, chown,
Apache pid under /var/run). TOS forbids root containers, so this wrapper runs
the unmodified FreshRSS app with a private, writable copy of the Apache config
as uid 1000 on port 8080.
descript: FreshRSS is a self-hosted RSS and Atom feed aggregator. Subscribe to feeds, organise them into categories, search and filter articles, and read them in a clean web UI. An optional API, off by default, connects mobile clients and other apps. This package runs the official Docker Hub image as a non-root container, and the database, users and extensions live in the application data folder.
release_note: 1.31.0-1: rectified per review comments. T1: base image upgraded to FreshRSS 1.31.0, a security release that fixes several critical vulnerabilities. C5: the Help link in the package config.ini now opens the bundled public privacy policy (PRIVACY.md) instead of the issue tracker URL. C8: the policy discloses every outbound endpoint with the data sent and the destination or region (subscribed feeds, favicon fetches, WebSub hubs, the GitHub extension catalogue and extension downloads), plus retention, user rights, security measures and the deletion channel. F5: the description now matches the delivered features (API optional and off by default, no background cron) and the entrypoint now prepares the data directories exactly like the official one, which fixes the first-run installer warnings and the broken favicon / API token storage.
important: Open the web UI and complete the first-run page to create the administrator account. There is no default password. Feed data and users live in DockerAppData/freshrssdocker/data, extensions in .../extensions. The image cron is not started in this non-root package, so feeds refresh on demand from the web UI or from an external scheduler. Needs DockerEngine. Back up data before uninstalling with data removal.

data_notes: `data` holds `config.php`, the SQLite database (or DB settings), users and feed caches; `extensions` holds installed FreshRSS extensions. Copying `data` and `extensions` is a complete backup.
design_notes: **Rootless Apache.** `src/entrypoint.sh` copies Apaches config to `/tmp`, changes the vhost to 8080, runs `cli/prepare.php` to create the data directories and starts Apache as uid 1000; the app code is unmodified.
**Two volumes, one port.** `/var/www/FreshRSS/data` + `/var/www/FreshRSS/extensions`; only port 8080 is published (host 8029).
**Health check** probes port 8080 inside the container.
**No root cron.** The images cron is not started because the container is non-root; feeds refresh on demand from the web UI or from an external scheduler.
**Hardening.** `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `no-new-privileges`, fixed image tag, Docker Hub only, no privileged mode, no host network, no Docker socket.
limitations: There is no default account. The first-run page is open until you create the administrator; complete it immediately after installation.
The API (Google Reader / Fever) is disabled by default. Enable it in the FreshRSS administration settings if you want mobile clients.
No automatic background refresh: the images cron needs root, so feeds refresh on demand from the web UI or from an external scheduler.
SQLite is used by default. Very large feed collections may benefit from an external database, which requires editing the configuration.
Plain HTTP on the LAN. Do not expose the published port to the internet without a TLS reverse proxy.
